lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Rebuilt weekly carrier scorecards used by 6 regional managers to renegotiate contracts, cutting late deliveries from 11% to 7% in two quarters.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Harbor Payments appears below the older Crestline Logistics role, so Experience is not in reverse chronological order.
items.because: A reader expects the more recent role first and may otherwise misread the timeline.

items.says: Education appears before substantial professional experience.
items.because: Leading with the MBA delays the evidence of the candidate’s work background.

items.says: The Coastal Marine Services entry should be shortened or removed if it does not support the product-focused target.
items.because: Its space can keep more relevant product evidence from standing out.

items.says: The five-day claim does not clarify what time it measures or what comparison makes it meaningful.
items.because: A reader cannot judge the turnaround claim without knowing what the time covers or how the rebuilds affected it.

items.says: The line attributes the delivery-rate improvement to the scorecards without establishing that they caused it.
items.because: Scorecards used in contract negotiations do not, by themselves, establish why delivery performance improved.

items.says: The line does not establish that the slotting redesign produced the 30% reduction in pick errors.
items.because: The rollout and retraining do not show how the reduction was measured or whether the redesign caused it.

items.says: The bullet uses a first-person pronoun and obscures who implemented the slotting change.
items.because: “My” shifts the bullet into first person, while “was rolled out with” leaves the implementation less direct.

items.says: The line attributes the forecast-error improvement to the consensus forecast without establishing that the process caused it.
items.because: Introducing the forecast does not, by itself, prove it reduced forecast error.

items.says: “For 12 consecutive quarters” is longer than needed to state the duration.
items.because: The emphasis does not change the reader’s understanding of the period.

items.says: The line does not establish how the annual driver-hours savings were calculated or whether the listed work produced them.
items.because: It gives no baseline or comparison supporting the figure or tying the changes to it.

items.says: The strongest outcome appears after a long list of activities.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the annual savings before reaching the end of the bullet.

items.says: The list of process details crowds the main accomplishment.
items.because: The procedure-writing, training and vendor-negotiation details compete with the rollout and savings for attention.

items.says: RICE Reach is scored with ticket counts rather than the estimated number of people or customers affected.
items.because: Repeat tickets from one person do not measure the number of people reached.

items.says: The dispute-roadmap bullets do not name the initiative chosen or what the decision changed.
items.because: A reader cannot judge the product or business significance of the prioritization.

items.says: The line names loss sizing but gives no estimate or segment comparison to show what the analysis found.
items.because: A reader cannot tell what evidence supported the roadmap decision.

items.says: The main roadmap decision is delayed until after a long list of research and analysis tasks.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the product decision the work supported.

items.says: The Harbor Payments entry repeats the same checkout A/B test and conversion lift in two bullets.
items.because: The earlier bullet reports the same test as a move from 61% to 66%, making the later bullet look like padding.

items.says: The funding outcome is stated indirectly through the leadership team.
items.because: Making the leadership team the grammatical subject makes the result less immediate.

items.says: The line claims all redistributed food would otherwise have been thrown away without establishing that counterfactual.
items.because: The amount redistributed does not show what would otherwise have happened to the food.

items.says: The launch bullet gives the app’s reach and partners but not your specific contribution to getting it live.
items.because: A reader cannot see what product or operational skill you brought to the launch.

items.says: The increase is 187.5%, not 150%.
items.because: Weekly active users rose by 750 from a starting point of 400.

items.says: The line attributes the increase in weekly active users to the reminders without evidence that they caused it.
items.because: The interviews do not rule out other changes or trends behind the before-and-after increase.

items.says: The change from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% increase.
items.because: Relative to the starting 75%, the increase is about 26.7%.

items.says: “Based on the model” does not identify the analysis or data supporting the savings estimate.
items.because: A reader cannot see the analytical work behind the figure.

items.says: The line gives no measure of how much the intake form was shortened.
items.because: A reader cannot gauge the size of the adopted change.

items.says: The passive construction leaves the team’s intake-mapping and form-shortening actions less direct.
items.because: “Was mapped” and “was shortened” make a reader infer the actions and ownership.
